data.name: AlertDiskUsageRaisedSubject
data.value: Disk space is running out on {0}

data.name: AlertDiskUsageRaisedBody
data.value: The filesystem {0} is {1}% full and has stayed above the threshold for ten consecutive checks. Free some space before writes start failing.

data.name: AlertDiskUsageResolvedSubject
data.value: Disk space has recovered on {0}

data.name: AlertDiskUsageResolvedBody
data.value: The filesystem {0} is back below the threshold, at {1}% full.

data.name: AlertServiceStoppedRaisedSubject
data.value: The service {0} has stopped

data.name: AlertServiceStoppedRaisedBody
data.value: The service {0} has been reported stopped for ten consecutive checks. The service manager says: {1}

data.name: AlertServiceStoppedResolvedSubject
data.value: The service {0} is running again

data.name: AlertServiceStoppedResolvedBody
data.value: The service {0} is running again. The service manager says: {1}

data.name: AlertSftpJailDriftedRaisedSubject
data.value: The SFTP jail configuration on this server has drifted

data.name: AlertSftpJailDriftedRaisedBody
data.value: The sshd configuration block that confines every SFTP login to its own files is missing or has been altered ({1}). Until it is restored, SFTP customers on this server are no longer confined to file transfer: their credentials can open an ordinary shell and reach anything a shell can reach, not only their own files. Restore the "Match Group" block that installer/lib/86-sftp.sh writes to /etc/ssh/sshd_config (or re-run the installer's SFTP setup step) and reload sshd.

data.name: AlertSftpJailDriftedResolvedSubject
data.value: The SFTP jail configuration on this server has been restored

data.name: AlertSftpJailDriftedResolvedBody
data.value: The sshd configuration block that confines every SFTP login to its own files is present and intact again. SFTP customers on this server are once more confined to file transfer only.

data.name: AlertQuotaNotEnforceableRaisedSubject
data.value: This server cannot enforce disk quotas

data.name: AlertQuotaNotEnforceableRaisedBody
data.value: The filesystem holding hosting accounts' home directories ({0}) cannot enforce a per-user disk quota ({1}), and has stayed that way for ten consecutive checks. Any disk allowance shown for accounts on this server is the plan's own figure and is not currently being applied — an account can use more than its plan allows. To restore enforcement, mount the filesystem with quota accounting (usrquota/uquota) and run quotacheck and quotaon; that is a decision for you to make on this host, and the panel will not do it for you.

data.name: AlertQuotaNotEnforceableResolvedSubject
data.value: This server can enforce disk quotas again

data.name: AlertQuotaNotEnforceableResolvedBody
data.value: The filesystem holding hosting accounts' home directories ({0}) can once again enforce a per-user disk quota. Disk allowances shown for accounts on this server are being applied again.

data.name: AlertCodeIntegrityDriftedRaisedSubject
data.value: Installed files on this server differ from what was released ({0})

data.name: AlertCodeIntegrityDriftedRaisedBody
data.value: The panel's own comparison of its installed files against the signed release it believes it is running found a difference, and has stayed that way for ten consecutive checks: {1}. This is a statement of fact, not an accusation — your license permits you to modify your own installation, and this notice does not claim otherwise. If this change was not made by you, review it; if it was, no action is needed.

data.name: AlertCodeIntegrityDriftedResolvedSubject
data.value: Installed files on this server match what was released ({0}) again

data.name: AlertCodeIntegrityDriftedResolvedBody
data.value: The panel's own comparison of its installed files against the signed release it believes it is running no longer finds a difference (or the comparison itself is working again): {1}.

data.name: AlertFreeSpaceFloorApproachingRaisedSubject
data.value: The server will soon refuse new work on {0}: free space is near the floor

data.name: AlertFreeSpaceFloorApproachingRaisedBody
data.value: The filesystem {0} has {1} GiB left, less than twice the free-space floor, and has stayed there for ten consecutive checks. Below the floor the server refuses to create accounts, take or restore backups and accept uploads. Free some space now.

data.name: AlertFreeSpaceFloorApproachingResolvedSubject
data.value: Free space on {0} is clear of the floor again

data.name: AlertFreeSpaceFloorApproachingResolvedBody
data.value: The filesystem {0} has {1} GiB left, at least twice the free-space floor.

data.name: AlertClockUnsynchronizedRaisedSubject
data.value: The server's clock is not synchronised

data.name: AlertClockUnsynchronizedRaisedBody
data.value: The server's clock is not synchronised with a time source ({1}), and has stayed that way for ten consecutive checks. Two-factor codes, sign-in sessions, certificates and the licence check all depend on the right time, and fail in confusing ways when the clock drifts. Enable a time synchronisation service on this host (systemd-timesyncd or chrony) and make sure it can reach a time server.

data.name: AlertClockUnsynchronizedResolvedSubject
data.value: The server's clock is synchronised again

data.name: AlertClockUnsynchronizedResolvedBody
data.value: The server's clock is synchronised with a time source again.
